newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss banks' net foreign assets set record in Q496.
newsitem.headline: Swiss banks' net foreign assets set record in Q496.

text.p: Net foreign assets held by Swiss banks and trust administrators rose to a record 138.2 billion Swiss francs at the end of 1996, partly as a result of the weaker Swiss franc, the Swiss National Bank said.
Net foreign assets held by 340 Swiss-based financial institutions rose 8.4 billion francs in the quarter, the SNB said in an advance summary of its March monthly report.
Balance-sheet claims against foreign banks and non-banks, including swaps with the SNB, rose by 54.5 billion francs from the end of September to the end of December to 365.4 billion.
"The significant increase can be traced in part to higher foreign exchange rates," it said. Money market rates were little changed in the quarter.
Claims against other banks abroad and lending to non-banks grew strongly, but holdings of foreign securities were steady.
"Divided into currencies, assets in dollars and other currencies -- with the exception of the mark -- grew strongly," it said. Assets in marks and francs dipped slightly in the quarter.
Securities lending grew sharply, up 7.9 billion Swiss francs to 32.4 billion. That represented growth of 14.4 billion in a year. Most of the borrowed securities came from domestic parties.
Liabilities against foreigners rose 49.4 billion Swiss francs in the quarter to 301.3 billion, led by liabilities to foreign banks. Customer deposits from abroad also rose.
"The surplus in balance-sheet items expanded as a result of these movements in the fourth quarter by 5.1 billion Swiss francs to 64.1 billion."
In the trusts sector, foreign assets rose by 28.5 billion Swiss francs to 396.3 billion, just below the record 408.4 billion set in March 1991. More than half of all foreign assets were in dollars.
Liabilities rose 25.2 billion Swiss francs to 322.2 billion, so that net foreign assets rose 3.3 billion to 74.1 billion in the quarter.
